title: Input engine: beforeinput router, inputType matrix, word coalescing
goal: Every user intent arrives via beforeinput (or a documented keydown fallback), is prevented, becomes a transaction, is appended to the ledger and rendered, with text and caret outcomes matching native behaviour per browser.
scope: docs/input-matrix.md lists every Input Events Level 2 inputType as handled / delegated / blocked with its test id

Handled here: insertText, insertReplacementText, insertLineBreak, insertParagraph, insertFromYank, insertTranspose, deleteContentBackward/Forward, deleteWordBackward/Forward, deleteSoftLineBackward/Forward, deleteEntireSoftLine, deleteHardLineBackward/Forward, deleteContent
Delegated: insertCompositionText (E1-009), historyUndo/Redo (E1-010), formatBold/Italic/Remove + insertUnorderedList (E1-011), insertFromPaste/PasteAsQuotation/Drop, deleteByCut/Drag (E1-012)
Blocked (preventDefault, no-op, tested): all other types; unknown types blocked with one console.warn
getTargetRanges() as the source of the browser’s own grapheme/word/line ranges; fallback via Intl.Segmenter + mapper
Selection-replacing input across blocks = one transaction (del + joins + ins)
Word-level coalescing (D14) with a buffered pending event
Enter splits the block; Shift+Enter inserts \n rendered as

rules.rule: preventDefault immediately; no native mutation survives.
Plain-text outcomes match the native oracle of the same browser (I4).
No keydown-based text insertion except documented fallbacks.

bar.primary: B1 native oracle (text + caret per browser)
secondary: B2 ProseMirror for Enter/Backspace at block boundaries
metrics: input → committed render p95 ≤ 4 ms desktop / ≤ 16 ms mobile on the 10k-word doc

criteria: input-matrix.md covers all L2 types; every handled type has ≥ 1 scenario per target, or "not emitted by this browser" is documented with evidence.
Plain-text corpus: final text and caret equal the native oracle on each of the 5 targets (0 divergences, or each divergence judged blind in our favour).
Fuzz without composition: 10 000 sequences per desktop target, 1 000 per mobile target, I1–I8 hold, 0 violations.
Typing "Hello wonderful world." produces 3–4 ledger events, never one per keystroke; 1 s idle and caret jumps flush.
Latency p95 ≤ 4 ms desktop and ≤ 16 ms mobile on the 10k-word doc.
macOS Ctrl+T (transpose) and Ctrl+K/Ctrl+Y (kill/yank) match native in WebKit and Chromium.
acceptance.critic: Differential (anonymized, divergences judged blind) plus criteria; the gap is the first lost divergence or unproven criterion.
